correctness.rationale: Invert the four partially entangled measurement-basis vectors explicitly: the four Bob unnormalized maps are unitarily equivalent to diag(x,y)/√2 or diag(y,x)/√2, with 1/√2≤x≤1, y=√(1−x²). For y>0, any branchwise success Kraus K reversing an unknown qubit to cU requires KD=cU and K†K≤I, hence |c|²≤y²/2 by the inverse operator norm. The filters Ks=diag(y/x,1) and Kf=diag(√(1−y²/x²),0) attain the bound and satisfy exact completeness. Four exclusive branches give 2y², including x=1/√2 probability 1 and x=1 probability 0 (in the latter case the inverse formula replaced by limiting/impossibility rank argument). Eq (9) printed second filter diag(1−y/x,0) does not satisfy Kraus completeness unless endpoint; correcting its matrix and decomposition is necessary. This is an analytic operator inequality, not an inference from numerical replay.
